thread.title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Turn Negative as Apple's Weak iPhone Sales Overshadow Upbeat CPI Data

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Turn Negative as Apple's Weak iPhone Sales Overshadow Upbeat CPI Data
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds in Wednesday's regular session:
VelocityShares 3x Inv Natural Gas ETN ( DGAZ ): -41%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): -0.6%
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): +0.8%
United States Oil Fund ( USO ): -2.5%
Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ): -0.7%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were lower. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ ( QQQ ) was down 0.7%.
US stocks reversed into negative territory at session's half, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average surrendering a triple-digit gain after another sell-off in component stock Apple (AAPL) tugged the blue chip index into the red for a fourth straight day. Weighed by analyst downgrades and worries about sluggish iPhone sales, Apple shares are trading at their lowest level since July and on the brink of bear-market territory.
Before the open, stock futures were inching higher as the rebound in oil futures coupled with gains in auto stocks set Wall Street up to break a three-day losing streak. Market-friendly inflation data helped drive the Dow more than 200 points higher at the open before worries about the outcome of the trade agreement between the US, Mexico and Canada, pressured the banking sector and fragile gains in the oil sector began to weigh.
Consumer prices increased an as-expected 0.3% last month and were up 0.2% excluding the volatile food and fuel segment. On an annual basis, the nominal CPI was up slightly from September's 2.3% to 2.5% while the core posted its smallest annual growth rate of 2.1% since February.
Power Play: Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was down 0.1% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was down 0.3%.
PG&E Corp. (PCG), the parent company of California utility Pacific Gas & Electric, saw its shares plunge nearly 23% after the firm disclosed it reported an incident last week on a transmission line in the state's Butte County on the day that the governor declared an emergency over a wildfire. In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission late Tuesday, the company said the cause of the so-called Camp Fire is under investigation. The state's fire authority, Cal Fire, said 42 people have been killed and the blaze is 30% contained. On Nov. 8, Pacific Gas and Electric "submitted an electric incident report to the California Public Utilities Commission" saying that at 6:15 am that day, the utility experienced an outage on the Caribou-Palermo 115 kV Transmission line in Butte County. In the afternoon of that same day, "PG&E observed by aerial patrol damage to a transmission tower" on the line, about a mile northeast of the town of Pulga, near the area of the Camp Fire. Acting Governor Gavin Newsom issued an emergency proclamation for Butte County, also on Nov. 8.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs (XLF) was down 1.3%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was down 2.9% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was up 3.3%.
NexPoint Residential Trust (NXRT) fell more than 1% after the firm priced a public offering of 2.35 million shares of its common stock at $33 per share for net proceeds of approximately $74 million. The price represents a discount of 4.4% from the stock's Nov. 13 closing price of $34.53. The company also granted the underwriters an option to purchase up to an additional 352,500 shares of its common stock in connection with the offering. NextPoint said it will contribute the net proceeds from the offering to NexPoint Residential Trust Operating Partnership, L.P., its operating partnership, which will use the net proceeds to repay the amount outstanding under its $30 million bridge facility and a portion of the amount outstanding under its $60 million credit facility. The offering is expected to close Nov. 16.
Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was down 1% and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW) and iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) were in the red.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) was up 0.8% and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) was up 0.5%.
Apple (AAPL) down almost 3% after several research firms and banks cut their outlook on the company. IPhone sales are expected to be slower than originally thought. Guggenheim downgraded the company, UBS cut its price target and Goldman Sachs said Tuesday in a note to clients that it lowered its forecasts for iPhone sales.
Commodities
Crude was down 4.3%. United States Oil Fund ( USO ) was down 2.6%. Natural gas was up 6.3% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was up 3.3%.
Gold was down 0.02%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was up 0.1%. Silver was up 0.1%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 0.3%.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was down 0.5% and Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Consumer Goods (IYK) were lower.
Meanwhile, Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was down 0.02% and retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were lower.
Automaker Ford Motor (F) and retail giant Walmart (WMT) said they are collaborating to explore delivery of grocery and other goods using self-driving vehicles. The companies will partner with San Francisco-based delivery service Postmates to design a service for autonomous-vehicle delivery of goods. As Postmates is already a partner of both Ford and Walmart, the companies noted that they will be able to utilize Postmates' infrastructure in the project. Walmart noted that in Miami, Postmates serves as it's delivery partner and is already connected to Ford's digital platform. Under a pilot program in Miami-Dade County, the companies will explore how to take advantage of self-driving vehicles to deliver everyday goods such as groceries, diapers, pet food and personal care items to customers. Ford and Walmart intend to use research vehicles, designed to simulate an autonomous experience, to gather crucial data about consumer preferences for grocery delivery. F shares were down 0.3% and WMT shares were down more than 1%.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was down 0.4% and other health care funds including Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Healthcare (IYH) were lower. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was down 1.8%.
Valeritas Holdings (VLRX) slumped by more than 18% intraday, earlier touching their lowest level ever, after the company said in Form S-1 filing it is offering for sale about 27.8 million shares of common stock, as well as Series A and B warrants for about $97.5 million.
